headline: Spanish Conjugation Patterns Foundation
threshold: Practice 28 named teaching patterns across 60 lessons, with ten distinct verbs and checked forms in every lesson.

lessons.title: Regular -ar present

words.en: I am a student of Spanish.

words.es: El curso es por la tarde.
words.en: The course is in the afternoon.

words.es: Somos seis personas en el grupo.
words.en: There are six of us in the group.

lessons.speaking: Use Regular -ar present while discussing identity and description. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing identity and description. Remove -ar; add -o, -as, -a, -amos, -an. Use the present for habits and current facts. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Regular -er present

words.en: I say my name when I enter.
What do you say when you do not understand?
We say that we need help.

lessons.speaking: Use Regular -er present while discussing saying and telling. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing saying and telling. Remove -er; add -o, -es, -e, -emos, -en. Notice nosotros ends in -emos. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Regular -ir present

words.es: Los libros están sobre la mesa.
words.en: The books are on the table.

lessons.speaking: Use Regular -ir present while discussing location and temporary conditions. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing location and temporary conditions. Remove -ir; add -o, -es, -e, -imos, -en. Nosotros distinguishes -ir from -er. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Present e → ie
lessons.objective: Present e → ie: Change the last stem e to ie in stressed forms; nosotros keeps e.

words.en: My brother is twenty years old.
Do you have time to eat?

lessons.speaking: Use Present e → ie while discussing possession and expressions. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing possession and expressions. Change the last stem e to ie in stressed forms; nosotros keeps e. The endings follow the infinitive family. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Present o → ue
lessons.objective: Present o → ue: Change the last stem o to ue in stressed forms; nosotros keeps o.

words.en: I do my homework at home.
What do you do after work?

lessons.speaking: Use Present o → ue while discussing doing and making. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing doing and making. Change the last stem o to ue in stressed forms; nosotros keeps o. Costar commonly describes a thing, not a person. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Present e → i
lessons.objective: Present e → i: These -ir verbs change the last stem e to i in stressed forms.

words.es: Hay una farmacia en esta calle.
words.en: There is a pharmacy on this street.

words.es: Hay dos personas en la entrada.
words.en: There are two people at the entrance.

words.es: No hay agua en la botella.
words.en: There is no water in the bottle.

words.es: He comprado pan para la cena.
words.en: I have bought bread for dinner.

lessons.speaking: Use Present e → i while discussing auxiliary haber and hay. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing auxiliary haber and hay. These -ir verbs change the last stem e to i in stressed forms. Nosotros keeps e. Seguir also loses u before o. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Present irregular yo in -go
lessons.objective: Present irregular yo in -go: Memorize the yo form in -go.

words.en: I go to the market on foot.

words.es: Mi amiga va a la estación.
words.en: My friend goes to the station.
We are going to buy fruit.

words.es: Después voy a preparar la cena.
words.en: Afterward I am going to prepare dinner.

lessons.speaking: Use Present irregular yo in -go while discussing going and planning. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing going and planning. Memorize the yo form in -go. Tener and venir also change e to ie; decir changes e to i; oír has y in several other persons. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Present yo in -zco
lessons.objective: Present yo in -zco: These selected verbs use -zco in yo and regular present endings elsewhere.

words.es: Veo las montañas desde mi ventana.
words.en: I see the mountains from my window.
Do you see the blue building?

words.es: Vemos a nuestros amigos los viernes.
words.en: We see our friends on Fridays.

words.es: Ellos ven el mapa en el teléfono.
words.en: They look at the map on the phone.

words.es: No veo bien sin mis lentes.
words.en: I cannot see well without my glasses.

lessons.speaking: Use Present yo in -zco while discussing seeing and watching. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing seeing and watching. These selected verbs use -zco in yo and regular present endings elsewhere. This is a teaching family, not a rule for every -cer or -cir verb. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Reflexive present
lessons.objective: Reflexive present: Match me, te, se, nos, se to the subject; put the pronoun before the conjugated verb.

words.es: Doy mi número a una compañera.
words.en: I give my number to a classmate.
She gives me a sheet of paper.
Will you give me a glass of water?

words.es: Mis vecinos dan un paseo por la tarde.
words.en: My neighbors go for a walk in the afternoon.

lessons.speaking: Use Reflexive present while discussing giving and fixed expressions. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing giving and fixed expressions. Match me, te, se, nos, se to the subject; put the pronoun before the conjugated verb. The infinitive ends in -se. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Plans: ir a + infinitive
lessons.objective: Plans: ir a + infinitive: Conjugate ir for the person, then add a and the unchanged infinitive.

words.es: Sé la dirección de la escuela.
words.en: I know the address of the school.
My sister knows how to swim.

words.es: No sabemos a qué hora empieza la clase.
words.en: We do not know what time the class begins.
Do you know where the stop is?
They know how to make this soup.

words.es: Ahora sé cómo llegar al centro.
words.en: Now I know how to get downtown.

lessons.speaking: Use Plans: ir a + infinitive while discussing knowing information and skills. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing knowing information and skills. Conjugate ir for the person, then add a and the unchanged infinitive. This construction describes plans or an approaching event. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.
